summary: Round-2 re-review of the documentation and evidence corrections at 869c2912c. The blocking round-1 finding KR-01 is resolved: the README headline (lines 3-4) now says "four workers, explicit 4 MiB task and 16 MiB bounce-buffer settings", the confirmation table row (line 67) is labelled "Exact datagrams, four-worker control", and the interpretation paragraph (lines 77-81) states that the earlier pipeline recorded only compatibility mode and four workers, did not capture effective task/bounce sizes, and that the 4/16 MiB values match installed library defaults, are explicitly set and verified in this test, and are not retrospective proof of unrecorded historical settings. A grep for "existing", "current settings", "original settings" and "historical" across the note directory finds no remaining instance of the old wording. The cross-reference paragraph added to notes/mfx_expand10_single_node_baseline_20261108.md (lines 122-129) uses the same "four workers, explicit 4 MiB tasks/16 MiB bounce buffers" phrasing and names the row a confirmed control, without any historical-settings claim. KR-02 is resolved by README lines 87-90, which state the control and eight-worker rows differ in both worker count and CPU-affinity count so no worker-count effect can be isolated, and that affinity values are logical CPU IDs with no recorded core/sibling topology. KR-04 is resolved: tests.log now opens with the working directory, interpreter, KVIKIO_READ_NATIVE_ROOT value and the unittest discovery command, followed by the unchanged 10-test OK output; the environment variable name matches test_audit.py line 11. KR-05 is resolved by the documentation alternative offered in round 1: README lines 25-27 mark the 524724-734604 range as manifest-derived and not a native report field, and request-size-evidence.json records the coordinator's manifest readback with generation SHA c45d191b... (matching the identity block in anchor-first.json, results.json and the 10k receipt files.json), per-file extrema whose sum 10000*(524724+629664+3*734604) equals 33,582,000,000 B, and 50,000 requests. KR-03 remains a deferred, non-blocking item: native reports are immutable, metric-definitions.json labels both input_direct_fd_count and the results.json alias direct_fd_count as a descriptor-flag census with no I/O-path evidentiary value, README lines 122-126 repeat this and state the key rename is deferred to a future benchmark version. Deferring the executable rename is acceptable; rerunning 33 measured GPU cases to rename an output key would add no evidentiary value. The 35 byte-identical evidence copies remain in build/read-evidence with copy-index.json listing 35 entries. No executable file or native report was claimed changed and none of the inspected executable snippets (read_case.py lines 58-75, plan_reads.py load_fixture) differ from the round-1 description. No new blocking issue found.
